headline: USC marching band benched for UCLA game after vandalism, officials say
author: Dhruti Shah

paragraphs.text: The 7LIVEDeveloping stories we're following
Reporter covering international breaking news

The University of Southern California’s marching band will not take the field during Saturday’s game against the University of California at Los Angeles, after three band members were arrested after an alleged vandalism incident, according to officials and local media reports.
Earlier this week, letters were removed from the sign at UCLA’s Wasserman Football Center ahead of a high-stakes football game at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California.

A photograph published by UCLA’s newspaper, the Daily Bruin, on Wednesday showed the sign reading: “Ass Football Center.” By that evening, it had been changed to Football Centre, the Los Angeles Times reported.
USC President Beong-Soo Kim said Wednesday that “individual students” from the Trojan Marching Band had been involved in a vandalism incident which he described as “unacceptable.”
Kim said that “out of respect for UCLA,” officials decided the USC band would not take the field for the traditional pregame and halftime performances.
The majority of the band’s 350 members would play from the stands, but band members linked to the UCLA incident would not attend, USC said Saturday.
Three people were arrested over the incident, local media reported, citing UCLA officials.
USC and UCLA have a long history of pranks before football games.
Reporter covering politics and breaking news
5.0-magnitude earthquake shakes Southern California
A 5.0-magnitude earthquake took place just off the coast of Southern California on Saturday morning local time, shaking nearby Los Angeles neighborhoods.
According to the U.S. Geological Survey, the quake took place at 9:30 a.m. Pacific time, about 3.7 miles west-southwest of Manhattan Beach.
There have been several aftershocks since the initial earthquake — including a 4.6-magnitude quake just before noon, according to USGS data.
The city of Manhattan Beach said on social media that there was no tsunami threat resulting from the quake and warned that aftershocks could occur.
The city is closing Manhattan Beach Pier until further notice as a precaution.
The earthquake also briefly disrupted operations at Los Angeles International Airport.

Live-stream footage monitoring airline arrivals at LAX on Saturday captured a plane attempting to land at the moment of the quake, with the camera’s shot shaking and car alarms going off. An air traffic controller is heard instructing the Delta plane to conduct a “go-around,” telling the flight crew, “We’re having a big earthquake.”
A plume of smoke was also seen at the nearby Chevron El Segundo refinery around the time of the initial earthquake.
Chevron spokesperson Ross Allen said the quake triggered automatic safety systems at the refinery, resulting in the use of the system’s safety flares.
“This unplanned utilization of the facility’s safety flare system does not pose a safety risk to the community,” Allen said.
College Board says it is investigating possible AI hack

College Board, the nonprofit organization that administers standardized tests and hosts an online application used to award financial aid, said that it suspects artificial intelligence tools were recently used to gain unauthorized access to students’ and professionals’ account information.
The organization disclosed the breach in a statement Friday, saying it “took immediate action” to protect its users and systems.

“Our preliminary assessment is that this activity involved sophisticated AI tools that have recently been leveraged to gain access to the systems of other major institutions worldwide,” College Board said in the statement. “While our investigation is ongoing, we have determined that the activity involved access to the systems students and professionals use to create new College Board accounts and to submit CSS Profile applications for financial aid.”

The organization did not disclose the scale of the breach or details on what data was accessed, but said it “allowed the actors to access basic account information for a subset of users and to initiate password resets in some cases.”

As of Saturday afternoon, College Board’s CSS Profile applications remained temporarily disabled in response to the suspicious activity. The organization said there is no evidence to suggest that its repository of test scores and content was improperly accessed.
Groupthink can be a good thing in browser tabs

The tab groups feature in a browser can bring order to the chaos of having dozens of pages opened in a browser window by letting you file pages about shared subjects (say, recipes or travel) in distinct collections. Every major browser supports them, with the option to open a link in a current or new tab group usually behind a contextual menu you bring up with a right-click or a long press of the screen.

Browsers differ, however, in how they synchronize tab groups between your computers. Apple’s Safari does this best, automatically syncing all of your tab groups between Mac, iPhone and iPad copies of that browser and making them accessible via a prominent toolbar icon. It’s at the top right corner in the macOS and iPadOS versions of Safari, at the bottom of the screen in iOS.

Google’s Chrome implements its tab group sync somewhat less elegantly, hiding access to your groups behind an item halfway down the catchall menu list you open via a vertical-ellipsis icon at the top right. Microsoft’s Edge, based on Chrome’s underlying code, works in much the same way except its menu icon is a horizontal ellipsis at the top right in its Mac and Windows apps and at the bottom right of its iOS and Android releases. Mozilla Firefox, however, doesn’t support tab-group sync, leaving it in last place in this feature ranking.
New York Mayor Mamdani underwent surgery to repair torn Achilles tendon
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) underwent surgery Friday to repair the Achilles tendon he tore during a soccer match last week.

Mamdani’s press secretary, Joe Calvello, said in a statement that the surgery, which lasted just over an hour, “was successful” and that the mayor is expected to make a full recovery. Mamdani was discharged from the hospital the same day as his procedure, Calvello said.
The 35-year-old mayor sustained the injury during a soccer match against local journalists Nov. 19. Mamdani’s team won the game, with the mayor scoring a goal.
At a news conference about closing the Rikers Island jail complex the following day, Mamdani acknowledged that he did not stretch before the game.

“I scored a goal soon after getting on the pitch, and I forgot that I was 35, and soon after I tore my Achilles, and I will be in a boot for six to eight weeks,” Mamdani told reporters. “And I will play soccer in about nine months.”
Since the incident, Mamdani has continued to make public appearances wearing a medical boot and using crutches.
The mayor’s office did not disclose where the surgery was done but thanked medical staff for the “first-class care” he received.
Executive producer of shows
Life Hax: Is it okay to NOT let guests bring plus-ones to my wedding?
What’s the etiquette for inviting guests to a wedding? Do you automatically include a plus-one for them?

One couple is weighing the rules as the two get ready for their own nuptial celebrations. And in this week’s episode of the “Life Hax” podcast, columnists Shane O’Neill and Carolyn Hax debate the options. (You can find the full episode, which includes more wedding-related dilemmas, on Apple Podcasts, Spotify and YouTube.)

Our letter writer notes that they’ve never needed a date to enjoy a wedding and think it’s “a little silly” to invite plus-ones. They’ve seen different approaches: “We’ve had friends who only invited the partners of guests who were married, engaged, or living together,” they wrote. But “that created way too many weird exclusions.”
So what’s a 30-something to do?
Shane proposes one rubric: “If you know their name and you would be embarrassed to run into them and be like, ‘I didn’t invite you to the wedding,’ invite them to the wedding!”
Carolyn calls that “brilliant.”
The guest list is more about finances than excluding people, Shane adds, because “by the time you’re drunk and doing the Chicken Dance, my worst enemy could be at my wedding.”
Reporter covering breaking news
Israeli strike on Gaza kills 2 Doctors Without Borders staff, charity says

Humanitarian charity Doctors Without Borders said an Israeli strike killed two of its staff members at a clearly marked Gaza City clinic on Friday — an attack the Israeli military said was targeted at Hamas members “under humanitarian cover.”
“We are devastated and outraged by the killing of two of our colleagues, both watchmen, in an Israeli strike on one of our Gaza clinics tonight,” the group said on X. “This is a direct hit on MSF.”

The Israel Defense Forces said in a statement Saturday that it killed “Hamas terrorists posing as humanitarian workers.” The military said that two men, whom it named, were working as security guards at the clinic operated by Doctors Without Borders “while also serving as terrorists,” without providing evidence. It added that no medical infrastructure in the area was damaged in the strike.
At least 17 members of Doctors Without Borders have been killed in Gaza since October 2023, the charity said.
According to the charity, the premises hit in the attack had been “clearly marked” with its logos and the location had been “communicated to and was known by” the Israeli military.

World Health Organization Director General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus wrote on X that attacks on health facilities, health workers and humanitarian personnel in Gaza are “outrageous and unacceptable.” He extended “heartfelt condolences” to Doctors Without Borders colleagues.
